mainTopic: Conflicting reports on אבא שאול and on רבי שמעון: whether a slave can be freed with money or only with a שטר
overview: רבי זירא tests two opposite reports about whether the הלכה follows אבא שאול. רבי יעקב בר אידי reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that it does. רבי חייא בר אבא reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that it does not. For each report, רבי זירא asks whether it was heard directly or worked out from רבי's ruling that a slave goes free only with a שטר. רבי יוחנן explained that ruling with a גזירה שוה comparing a slave to a wife. רבי זירא shows that this comparison can be stretched in either direction, and both reporters answer that they heard their ruling directly. The גמרא then asks how רבי can say 'only a שטר' when another ברייתא has him letting a slave buy himself free. It answers that money or a שטר usually works, but here the master's money hold is already gone. This general rule rejects רבי שמעון in the name of רבי עקיבא, who learns from a פסוק that only a שטר fully frees a slave. Reports differ on whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. A story about רב נחמן and a master's hat turns out to rest on a different reason (כליו של מקנה), and the גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון. The amud ends by opening a new case: an עבד who marries a free woman in front of his master, with the ruling on the next amud.

steps.title: Did you hear it directly or work it out?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי יעקב בר אידי whether his report from רבי יהושע בן לוי was said outright or was his own inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did you hear it said outright, or did you work it out from something else he said?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is checking the source of a ruling reported in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי. He wants to know whether it was said openly or only inferred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inference from another statement is weaker than a direct quote, because the inference might be mistaken. This question sets up the whole discussion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, worked out from a general statement

phrases.english: Did you hear it explicitly,
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is asking רבי יעקב בר אידי about the ruling he reported, that the הלכה follows אבא שאול.

phrases.english: or did you hear it by inference?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפֵירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ, אוֹ מִכְּלָלָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling like אבא שאול was said outright or only inferred.

steps.title: What inference could there be?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי asks which statement he could have inferred it from.
steps.simpleTranslation: What inference do you mean?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אידי asks רבי זירא which statement could even lead to such an inference. This line sets up רבי זירא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא must now show a real statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי that could lead someone to the ruling of אבא שאול.

phrases.english: What inference?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כְּלָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the inference mentioned in step 1 refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which other statement could have been the basis for an inference.

steps.title: רבי rules that a renounced slave needs a document
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reports that רבי ruled a master who gives up hope on his slave can free him only through a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: They asked רבי, 'If a master says, I have given up hope of getting back my slave so-and-so, what is the law?' He answered, 'I say his only remedy is through a document.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא names the statement that could be the source of the inference. It is רבי's ruling that a slave goes free only through a written document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving up hope (יאוש) on the slave does not set him free by itself. He still needs a שטר שחרור. This statement is the first link in the chain of reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: I have despaired, I have given up hope
A remedy, a way to fix the situation
A document, here a bill of freedom

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said,
they said before Rabbi:
If one said, 'I have despaired of so-and-so my slave,' what is the law?
He said to them: I say,
he has no remedy except through a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, אָמְרוּ לִפְנֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by naming the source of the possible inference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע בן לוי's report that רבי requires a שטר to free a slave whose master has given up on him.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains: a slave is compared to a wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי's reason is a גזירה שוה on the word 'לה', so a slave, like a wife, is released only with a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What is רבי's reason? He learned 'לה' from 'לה' written about a wife. Just as a wife is released through a document, so too a slave is freed through a document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי's ruling. This explanation links a slave to a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לה' appears in a verse about a slave woman and in a verse about divorce. That shared word teaches that a slave, like a wife, needs a written document to be released. This link between slave and wife is what makes the next inference possible.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned or derived it, here through a גזירה שוה
To her or for her, the shared word in the two verses

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi?
He derived 'lah' from 'lah' written about a wife –
phrases.notes: One 'לה' is from ויקרא 19:20 about a slave woman; the other is from דברים 24:3 about divorce.

phrases.english: just as a wife is released through a document,
so too a slave is also freed through a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural reason for רבי's ruling in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through the גזירה שוה of 'לה', a slave is compared to a wife: both are released through a written document.

steps.title: The inference: like a wife, a slave is freed from איסור but not ממון
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests that רבי יעקב בר אידי stretched the comparison: a master's death frees a slave from the איסור but not from the ממון bond, which matches אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you inferred from this that a slave is like a wife: just as a wife is released from a prohibition and not from a money bond, so too a slave is released from a prohibition and not from a money bond.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא spells out the inference he suspects רבי יעקב בר אידי made. The comparison to a wife would lead to the ruling of אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a husband dies, his wife's tie to him is a matter of איסור, and that is released. If a slave is like a wife, his master's death releases only the איסור, while the ממון bond stays. That fits אבא שאול's view that an adult slave and a minor slave are treated differently.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two comparisons. Step 4 compares slave and wife about needing a document. This step stretches that same comparison to a new question: what happens when the master dies.

phrases.english: And you deduced from it that he is like a wife –
just as a wife is released from a prohibition and not a money bond,
phrases.notes: He means what a husband's death releases her from.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עֶבֶד נָמֵי אִיסּוּרָא וְלָא מָמוֹנָא.
phrases.english: so too a slave is released from a prohibition and not a money bond.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָא דָיְיקַתְּ מִינַּהּ, כְּאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי יוחנן's slave-wife comparison to reach אבא שאול's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The suspected inference: slave like wife, so a master's death frees from איסור but not from ממון, which matches אבא שאול.

steps.title: So what if it was an inference?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי asks what would be wrong with the ruling if it came by inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was by inference, what of it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אידי asks what the problem would be with an inference. This sets up רבי זירא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is asking רבי זירא to show why that inference would not hold up.

phrases.english: And if by inference, what of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִכְּלָלָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the inference in step 5 would be a problem.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an inferred ruling would be unreliable here.

steps.title: The comparison can point the other way
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא argues that the comparison to a wife could just as easily teach that both adult and minor slaves go free when the master dies, which is against אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: On the contrary! Infer from it the other way: just as a wife is released whether she is an adult or a minor, so too a slave goes free whether he is an adult or a minor!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא shows that the inference is not reliable. The same comparison can lead to the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife is released by her husband's death at any age. If a slave is truly like a wife, then a minor slave should go free just like an adult, and that goes against אבא שאול. Since the comparison can point either way, an inference from it cannot prove the ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: A comparison (here, slave like wife) that can be pushed in two opposite directions cannot prove which direction is correct.

phrases.english: He said to him: On the contrary!
Deduce from it to the other side:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אִשָּׁה – בֵּין גְּדוֹלָה בֵּין קְטַנָּה,
phrases.english: just as a wife, whether adult or minor, is released,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עֶבֶד נָמֵי – בֵּין גָּדוֹל בֵּין קָטָן!
phrases.english: so too a slave goes free, whether adult or minor!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַדְּרַבָּה! דּוֹק מִינַּהּ לְאִידַּךְ גִּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by showing that the inference in step 5 can be reversed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the slave-wife comparison to אבא שאול's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wife is released at any age, so the comparison would free a minor slave as well. That reverses the inference and contradicts אבא שאול.

steps.title: I heard it explicitly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי answers that he heard the ruling like אבא שאול directly, not by inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I heard it explicitly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אידי answers the original question. He heard the ruling stated outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ruling was said directly, רבי זירא's challenge to the inference does not weaken it. The report that the הלכה follows אבא שאול stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling like אבא שאול was heard directly from רבי יהושע בן לוי, so it does not depend on the slave-wife comparison.
steps.whyThisMatters: A direct tradition from a teacher outweighs a logical inference that could be argued either way.

phrases.english: He said to him: I heard it explicitly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּפֵירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion by answering step 1 directly, which makes the challenge in step 7 irrelevant.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling like אבא שאול was heard explicitly from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling like אבא שאול rests on a direct tradition, not an inference.

steps.title: A second report: the הלכה is not like אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה does not follow אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה is not like אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report, this time in the name of רבי יוחנן. It says the opposite of what רבי יעקב בר אידי reported in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יעקב בר אידי reported in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows אבא שאול. Now רבי חייא בר אבא reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that it does not. This sets up a clash between two reports, and the גמרא will test this one just as it tested the first.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law is not (like this opinion)
The תנא whose view about a slave whose master dies is being discussed

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba says that Rabbi Yochanan says:
The halacha is not like Abba Shaul.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite ruling in the name of רבי יוחנן, after the ruling in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי was confirmed as heard directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי חייא בר אבא, רבי יוחנן ruled that the הלכה is not like אבא שאול.

steps.title: Did you hear it directly or work it out?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי חייא בר אבא whether he heard this ruling directly or worked it out himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי חייא בר אבא: Did you hear it explicitly, or did you hear it by inference?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks רבי חייא בר אבא the same question he asked רבי יעקב בר אידי: did רבי יוחנן say this outright, or did you figure it out yourself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling heard word for word is much stronger than one worked out from something else the teacher said. If רבי חייא בר אבא only worked it out, רבי זירא can test whether that reasoning really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; worked out from a general statement

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
Did you hear it explicitly,
or did you hear it by inference?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפֵירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ, אוֹ מִכְּלָלָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how reliable the report in step 9 is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן said this ruling outright or רבי חייא בר אבא worked it out from another teaching.

steps.title: The possible source: רבי's ruling about giving up on a slave
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא asks what inference he could have made. רבי זירא points to רבי's ruling that a slave whose master has given up on him can only go free with a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: What inference? רבי יהושע בן לוי said: They asked רבי, if someone says, "I have given up on so-and-so, my slave," what is the law? He said to them: I say he has no fix except through a document.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא asks what inference רבי זירא means. רבי זירא starts laying out the chain of reasoning, beginning with רבי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ruled that even if a master gives up on his slave, the slave still needs a שטר to go free. This is the first link in the chain; the next step brings רבי יוחנן's reason for it.

keyTerms.meaning: I have given up hope (of getting him back)
A document; here, a document freeing a slave

phrases.english: What inference?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, אָמְרוּ לִפְנֵי רַבִּי:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: They said before Rabbi:
"I have despaired of so-and-so, my slave," what is the law?
He said to them: I say,
he has no remedy except through a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כְּלָלָא? דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the 'inference' from step 10 could be built on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The inference would start from רבי's ruling that a slave can only go free with a שטר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason: a slave is compared to a wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא continues: רבי יוחנן explained that רבי learned this from the word 'לה' that appears for both a wife and a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: What is רבי's reason? He learned "לה" from "לה" said about a wife. Just as a wife goes free through a document, a slave also goes free through a document.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings the second link in the chain: רבי יוחנן's גזירה שוה linking a slave to a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same teaching quoted earlier in step 4. The גמרא repeats it here because it is the base of רבי חייא בר אבא's possible inference. Once a slave is compared to a wife, someone might stretch the comparison further.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned from the shared word 'לה' (a גזירה שוה)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: What is the reason of Rabbi?
He derived "to her" from "for her" said about a wife.
phrases.notes: The word לה appears about a freed maidservant and also about a divorced wife; the shared word links the two.

phrases.english: Just as a wife goes out through a document,
so too a slave goes out through a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יוחנן's reason for רבי's ruling, finishing the base of the inference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי's ruling rests on a גזירה שוה comparing a slave to a wife.

steps.title: The inference: adult or minor, both go free
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests רבי חייא בר אבא stretched the comparison: a wife goes free at her husband's death whether adult or minor, so a slave should too, which goes against אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you deduced from this that a slave is like a wife: just as a wife goes free whether she is an adult or a minor, a slave also goes free whether he is an adult or a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא spells out the inference he thinks רבי חייא בר אבא made, ending with a ruling against אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a slave is like a wife, then a master's death should work for a slave the way a husband's death works for a wife. That applies whether the slave is an adult or a minor, with no difference. This leads to 'the הלכה is not like אבא שאול', exactly what רבי חייא בר אבא reported.

phrases.english: And you deduced from it: like a wife,
phrases.notes: Here the comparison is about what happens when the master dies, like a husband's death.

phrases.aramaic: מָה אִשָּׁה בֵּין גְּדוֹלָה בֵּין קְטַנָּה,
phrases.english: just as a wife, whether adult or minor, goes free,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עֶבֶד נָמֵי בֵּין גָּדוֹל בֵּין קָטָן.
phrases.english: so too a slave, whether adult or minor, goes free.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָא דָיְיקַתְּ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws from step 12's comparison the conclusion רבי חייא בר אבא might have reached.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The suspected inference: a slave, adult or minor, goes free at the master's death like a wife does, which goes against אבא שאול.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the mirror image of steps 5-8. There, רבי זירא suggested the comparison led toward אבא שאול; here he suggests it led away from him. Same source, opposite stretch.

steps.title: So what if it was an inference?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא asks what would be wrong if he did learn it by inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was by inference, what of it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא asks why an inference would be a problem. This sets up רבי זירא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is asking whether the inference is actually weak. רבי זירא will now show it can be turned around.

keyTerms.meaning: And if by inference, so what?

phrases.english: And if it was by inference, what of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִכְּלָלָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what is wrong with the inference laid out in steps 11-13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the flaw would be in relying on the inference.

steps.title: The comparison can cut the other way
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא argues the opposite: a husband's death frees a wife from an איסור but not from a money bond, so a master's death would free a slave from the איסור only, which matches אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Infer from it in the other direction: just as a wife is released from an איסור and not from a money bond, a slave too is released from an איסור and not from a money bond!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא shows that the same comparison can lead to the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a husband dies, the wife is released from the איסור of marriage. This is not a release from a money bond. Applied to a slave, the master's death would release only the איסור, not the money bond, which fits אבא שאול. Since the comparison points both ways, it cannot prove that the הלכה goes against אבא שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: Infer from it in the other direction
Money; a financial bond of ownership

phrases.english: On the contrary! Infer from it to the other side:
just as a wife is released from a prohibition and not from money,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עֶבֶד נָמֵי – אִיסּוּרָא וְלָא מָמוֹנָא!
phrases.english: so too a slave is released from a prohibition and not from money!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה! דּוֹק מִינַּהּ לְהָךְ גִּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by showing the step 13 inference can be reversed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference in step 13 that the comparison to a wife rules against אבא שאול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same comparison can just as easily show that a master's death releases only the איסור, which supports אבא שאול. An inference that points both ways proves nothing.

steps.title: I heard it directly
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא answers that he heard the ruling from רבי יוחנן outright.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I heard it explicitly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers רבי זירא's challenge: he did not work it out; רבי יוחנן said it plainly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes רבי זירא's challenge, just as רבי יעקב בר אידי did in step 8. Now both reports are direct traditions: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules like אבא שאול, and רבי יוחנן rules against him.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יעקב בר אידי reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows אבא שאול. רבי חייא בר אבא reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that it does not. רבי זירא tested each to see whether he worked it out from the 'לה–לה' comparison. That comparison can be stretched either way, so it proves nothing. Both answered that they heard the ruling directly.

phrases.english: He said to him: I heard it explicitly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּפֵירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge in step 15 by saying the ruling was heard outright.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חייא בר אבא heard 'the הלכה is not like אבא שאול' directly from רבי יוחנן, not by inference.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because both reports were heard directly, the conflict stands as a real disagreement between רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן about אבא שאול.

steps.title: Quoting רבי: only a document can free him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to quote רבי's line from the earlier ברייתא: this slave can only be freed with a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said above: רבי told them, 'I say he has no fix except through a document.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the earlier ברייתא so it can examine it. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said that this slave has only one way out: a שטר שחרור. The words 'only through a document' sound like money can never free a slave. That is exactly what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said: the גמרא is quoting an earlier source to look at it closely
A fix, a way out of the problem
A document. Here it means a שטר שחרור, a document that frees the slave

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This refers back to the ברייתא the גמרא quoted earlier.

phrases.english: He said to them: I say,
he has no remedy except through a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי זירא and רבי חייא בר אבא exchange and goes back to examine a line in the earlier ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, this slave can only be freed through a שטר.

steps.title: Another source says רבי lets a slave buy himself free
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא has רבי saying the slave can pay his own value and go free, so money does work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that רבי says: 'I say, he too can pay his own value and go free, because it is as if he was sold to himself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the quote from רבי by bringing a different ברייתא where רבי says money can free a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 רבי said 'only a document.' Here רבי says the slave can pay his own worth and go out free, as if he were bought by himself. So does רבי think money works or not?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? This is a common way to open a challenge
His own value, the money he is worth
As if he was sold to himself

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi says:
I say, even he himself
gives his own value and goes free,
because it is as if he sold him to himself!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the quote of רבי from step 17 with a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's statement that the slave can only go free through a שטר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In another ברייתא רבי himself says a slave can go free by paying money, so 'only a document' contradicts רבי's own view.

steps.title: Money or document in general, but here the money hold is gone
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that a slave can usually go free with money or a שטר. In this case, though, the owner's money hold has already ended, so only a שטר is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: usually either money or a document works. But in this case, his money hold has already ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both quotes of רבי are true, because they talk about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general רבי agrees that a slave can go free with money or with a שטר. In the case of the earlier ברייתא, the owner's money claim on the slave is already gone, so there is nothing left to pay for. Only the שטר can finish freeing him.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means: the גמרא is explaining a statement so it fits

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not saying money never frees a slave. He is only saying it cannot work here, because the money side of the ownership is already gone.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
either through money or through a document;
and this one, his money hold has ended.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18 by separating the general rule from the special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a general rule versus this special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'only a document' meant רבי never lets money free a slave.
steps.terutzMaskana: Usually money or a שטר works. Here the owner's money hold has already ended, so only a שטר can free him.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's view: only a document fully frees
steps.stepSummary: The general rule 'money or a document' rejects the view of רבי שמעון in the name of רבי עקיבא. He learns from the פסוק of a שפחה חרופה that only a שטר fully frees, and money does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rejects the view of a certain תנא. A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון said in the name of רבי עקיבא: 'You might think money fully frees her, just like a document does. That is why the פסוק says, "and not at all redeemed." The whole passage is tied to "nor was freedom given to her," to teach you that a document fully frees her and money does not.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי's general rule disagrees with a ברייתא of רבי שמעון, who says in the name of רבי עקיבא that money cannot fully free a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names two things, being redeemed with money and being given freedom. רבי עקיבא notices that the law of the whole passage depends on the second one, freedom given with a שטר. That shows a שטר completes her freedom, while money does not, unlike רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: And this rejects, this comes to exclude another view
Completes her freedom, fully frees her
And not at all redeemed: about money
Tied it to, made it depend on
Nor was freedom given to her: about the שטר

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: a slave can go free with money or with a שטר, unless the owner's money hold has already ended. רבי שמעון in the name of רבי עקיבא: only a שטר fully frees, money does not.

phrases.english: And this excludes the view of this תנא –

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
You might think money completes her freedom,
just as a document completes it?
The verse says: "and not at all redeemed" –
it tied the entire passage
to "nor was freedom given to her,"
phrases.notes: These are the next words in the same פסוק. The law of the passage depends on these words, not on 'redeemed.'

phrases.english: to tell you: a document completes her freedom,
and money does not complete her freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַפּוֹקֵי מֵהַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows which other view is rejected by the general rule from step 19, that money or a שטר frees a slave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון in the name of רבי עקיבא, only a שטר fully frees a slave, and money does not. He learns this from the words לא חופשה in ויקרא 19:20.

steps.title: Two opposite reports on following רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא reports in the name of רב נחמן that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. רב יוסף בר חמא reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said in the name of רב נחמן: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. רב יוסף בר חמא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks what the practical הלכה is regarding רבי שמעון's view from the last step. Two reports disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that only a שטר fully frees a slave and money does not. רב נחמן is reported to agree with him, while רבי יוחנן is reported to reject him. This sets up the investigation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical ruling follows this person
The ruling does not follow him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said that Rav Nachman said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's view from the last step: only a שטר fully frees a slave, not money.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rav Yosef bar Chama said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha does not follow Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on רבי שמעון's view from step 20, and the ruling is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. רבי יוחנן: it does not.

steps.title: Asking which ruling is correct
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק meets רבא בר שאילתא at the entrance of a בית תפילה and asks him whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק found רבא בר שאילתא standing at the entrance of a house of prayer. He asked him: is it the הלכה or not the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. Someone asks directly which side of the dispute is the real הלכה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the reports in step 21 conflict, רב נחמן בר יצחק wants to know the true ruling. The question refers to רבי שמעון's view about freeing a slave only with a שטר.

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא בַּר שְׁאֵילְתָא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak found Rava bar She'eilta,
who was standing at the entrance of a house of prayer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲלָכָה אוֹ אֵין הֲלָכָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: Is it the halacha, or is it not the halacha?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲלָכָה אוֹ אֵין הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which of the two conflicting reports in step 21 is correct.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: His own view, and a report from מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שאילתא says that in his view the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון. He adds that the רבנן from מחוזא report, through רבי זירא, that רב נחמן said it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I say it is not the הלכה. But the רבנן who came from מחוזא say that רבי זירא said in the name of רב נחמן: it is the הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר שאילתא answers. He gives his own opinion and admits that there is a report in the name of רב נחמן saying the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report in רב נחמן's name is now confirmed by a second chain, through רבי זירא. That makes it serious, so the next step checks what רב נחמן actually said and did.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנִי אוֹמֵר – אֵין הֲלָכָה;
phrases.english: He said to him: I say it is not the halacha;
but the Rabbis who came from Mechoza say

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה;
phrases.english: that Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav Nachman: it is the halacha;

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנִי אוֹמֵר – אֵין הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In his own view the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון, but there is a report from רב נחמן that it does.

steps.title: Asking for the real story behind רב נחמן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שאילתא continues: when he came to סורא, he asked רבי חייא בר אבין to tell him exactly what happened in the case where רב נחמן ruled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when I came to סורא, I found רבי חייא בר אבין. I said to him: Tell me, my friend, what exactly happened in the actual incident?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר שאילתא is still talking. He wants the facts of the actual case, because a ruling only makes sense if you know what happened. This sets up the story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report that רב נחמן follows רבי שמעון probably came from a ruling in a real case. By asking for the facts, רבא בר שאילתא can check whether the ruling really depended on רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: סורא, a major Torah center in Bavel
My friend (a friendly way of addressing someone)

phrases.english: And when I came to Sura,
phrases.notes: The "I" here is still רבא בר שאילתא, telling his story.

phrases.english: I found Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin,
I said to him: Tell me, my friend,
how did the actual incident happen?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא לִי אִיזִי, גּוּפָא דְעוֹבָדָא הֵיכִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the report about רב נחמן in step 23 by asking for the facts of the case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact facts of the case in which רב נחמן ruled.

steps.title: The story of the master's hat
steps.stepSummary: A dying master's maidservant cried to him to be freed. He threw her his hat and told her to acquire it and thereby acquire herself. רב נחמן ruled that this did nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told me: There was a maidservant whose master was dangerously ill. She came crying to him and said: How long will that woman stay enslaved? He took his hat, threw it to her, and said: Go acquire this, and acquire yourself. They came to רב נחמן, and he said: He did nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבין tells the actual story. The master tried to free his maidservant by giving her his hat, and רב נחמן said she was not freed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No שטר was written here. The master used an act of acquisition with an object. רב נחמן said it failed, and that could look like proof that only a שטר works, as רבי שמעון holds. The next step checks whether that is really the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is dangerously ill and may be dying
He did nothing at all; the act has no effect

phrases.english: He said to me: There was a certain maidservant
whose master was dangerously ill,
she came crying before him and said to him:

phrases.aramaic: עַד אֵימַת תִּשְׁתַּעְבֵּיד וְתֵיזִיל הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא?
phrases.english: Until when will that woman go on being enslaved?
phrases.notes: "That woman" is a polite way of saying "me." She is talking about herself.

phrases.english: He took his hat and threw it to her,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: זִיל קְנִי הָא וּקְנִי נַפְשִׁיךְ.
phrases.english: and said to her: Go acquire this, and acquire yourself.
They came before Rav Nachman,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְלוּם.
phrases.english: and he said to them: He did nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לִי: דְּהַהִיא אַמְתָּא דַּהֲוָה מָרַהּ שְׁכִיב מְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the facts requested in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The master tried to free her with his hat, and רב נחמן ruled the act was invalid.

steps.title: The real reason for רב נחמן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: People who saw the case thought רב נחמן ruled this way because he follows רבי שמעון. The truth is different: the act failed because the item used belonged to the one giving up ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever saw it thought it was because the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. But that is not so. It was because the object used belonged to the one giving up ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב נחמן's ruling is not proof that he follows רבי שמעון. The ruling had a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this kind of acquisition by exchange (חליפין), the object has to come from the person receiving the ownership, not from the person giving it up. Here the master gave his own hat, so the act failed for that reason alone. This removes the basis for the report that רב נחמן ruled like רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: The object of the one giving up ownership

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's ruling in the hat case does not show that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. The act failed only because the master used his own hat. In this kind of exchange, the object must come from the one receiving ownership.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that "he did nothing" means only a שטר can free a slave. The failure came from the way the acquisition was done, not from a rule that only a שטר works.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a key method: before using a ruling as proof, find out the exact facts and the real reason behind it.

phrases.english: Whoever saw it thought
that it was because the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon;
but that is not so,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ כֵּלָיו שֶׁל מַקְנֶה.
phrases.english: rather, it was because it was the object of the one giving up ownership.
phrases.notes: In this kind of exchange, the object has to belong to the one receiving ownership. Here the hat was the master's own.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דַּחֲזָא, סָבַר מִשּׁוּם דַּהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן; וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the real reason for the ruling in the story from step 25. This undercuts the report in steps 21 and 23 that רב נחמן follows רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רב נחמן's ruling as proof that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling had a different reason: the object used belonged to the one giving up ownership.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן's ruling came from כליו של מקנה, not from following רבי שמעון. So the story is no proof that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: A long chain reports that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אחיתאי quotes a chain of teachers going back to רב המנונא, who said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אחיתאי said that רב המנונא סבא said that רבי יצחק בר אשיאן said that רב הונא said that רב המנונא said: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another report on the question from earlier steps. This time a long chain of teachers says the הלכה does follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא בר שאילתא held that the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון. The גמרא also showed that the case people linked to רב נחמן had a different reason. Here a separate tradition says the opposite: the הלכה does follow רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical law follows this opinion
The elder; used to tell apart two rabbis with the same name
"Said ... said": a chain of teachers, each passing the teaching to the next

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Aḥittai said,
Rav Hamnuna the Elder said,
phrases.notes: There are two people named רב המנונא in this chain. "The Elder" tells you this is a different one from the last name in the chain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Ashyan said,
Rav Huna said,
Rav Hamnuna said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַחִיתַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 26 removed the proof from רב נחמן's case, this step brings a separate chain of teachers that does rule like רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון, according to this chain of teachers.

steps.title: The גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the chain's report and decides that the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so: the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא speaks in its own voice and rejects what the long chain just said. The final ruling is that the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "ולא היא" are the גמרא's way of saying a report is wrong. Even a long chain of teachers does not settle the matter. The final ruling agrees with what רבא בר שאילתא held at the start of this discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: "But it is not so": the גמרא rejects the statement it just quoted
The law does not follow (this opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: Final ruling: the הלכה does NOT follow רבי שמעון. This matches רבא בר שאילתא's view, and the case of רב נחמן had a different reason.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop reading after step 27. The long chain says the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, but the גמרא immediately rejects it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for the whole רבי שמעון discussion on this page.

phrases.english: But that is not so;
the halakha does not follow Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the report given in step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole claim of step 27.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The report that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון is not the accepted ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון.

steps.title: A new ruling begins: an עבד who marries a free woman in front of his master
steps.stepSummary: A chain going back to רבי opens a new case: an עבד who marries a בת חורין while his master is present. The ruling comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said that רבי חנינא said that רב אשי said that רבי said: an עבד who married a free woman in front of his master...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and sets up a new case. It describes the situation here, and the ruling itself comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The master watches his עבד marry a free Jewish woman and does not object. The question is what the master's presence means for the עבד's status. The answer is given right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jewish master

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Ḥanina said
that Rav Ashi said that Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: A slave who married a free woman
in the presence of his master –

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא, אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אָמַר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The רבי שמעון discussion has ended. This step starts a new case about freeing an עבד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Describes the case of an עבד who married a free woman in front of his master. The ruling continues in the next part of the text.
